entries.meaning: O lord of birds, when the mighty sun of Rama's majesty arose, its light filled all three worlds. It brought joy to many but sorrow to those I shall name: first the night of ignorance vanished; the owls of sin hid wherever they could; the night-lotuses of desire and anger closed. The chakora-birds of diverse actions, qualities, times and dispositions found no delight, while the thieves envy, prestige, delusion and pride lost every trick. In the pond of dharma, the lotuses of knowledge and realization bloomed in manifold ways; happiness, contentment, detachment and discernment became innumerable cakravaka birds released from grief.

Once Rama went with his brothers and his supremely dear Hanuman to see a lovely grove, where every tree was flowering and putting out new leaves. Knowing the moment, Sanaka and the other ancient sages arrived: radiant masses of virtue and gracious conduct, forever absorbed in the bliss of Brahman, age-old yet appearing as children, like the four Vedas embodied. Equal-sighted and beyond distinctions, they have only this longing, dress and passion—to hear Raghupati's deeds wherever they are told. O Bhavani, they had been staying with the wise sage Agastya, who had narrated Rama's story at length; like fire born from fire-sticks, it is the source of knowledge.

All three brothers and Hanuman prostrated, overflowing with joy. Beholding Raghupati's incomparable beauty, the sages were so absorbed that they could not restrain their minds. They gazed unwinking at his dark body and lotus eyes, the abode of beauty and liberator from existence; before the Lord they kept their hands joined and heads bowed. Seeing their state, Raghubira's eyes streamed and his body thrilled. Taking their hands, he seated the eminent sages and spoke most graciously: ‘Listen, lords of sages: today I am blessed. At your sight sins waste away. Only through great good fortune is holy company obtained; without effort it breaks the bondage of existence.’

Hearing the Lord's words, the four delighted sages thrilled bodily and offered praise: ‘Victory to the Lord—infinite, free of affliction, sinless, many and one, compassionate; beyond qualities yet the ocean of virtues, the lovely and accomplished abode of joy. Victory to Lakshmi's beloved, bearer of the earth, peerless unborn and beginningless source of beauty; treasury of knowledge, without pride yet giver of honour, sanctifying glory proclaimed by Purana and Veda; knower of truth and of every deed, destroyer of ignorance, bearing many names yet nameless and stainless. You are everything, all-pervading, dwelling in every heart. Abide forever in us and protect us completely. Destroy dualities and calamities and sever worldly snares; dwelling in our hearts, Rama, crush desire and pride.’

‘Raghupati, grant us the supremely purifying devotion that destroys the oppression of worldly existence and its three afflictions. Be gracious and give this boon—you are the wish-granting cow and tree for those who bow to you; Agastya to the ocean of becoming, readily accessible to those who serve and giver of every joy; destroyer of the terrible pain born in the mind, friend of the lowly and extender of impartial grace; remover of hope, fear, envy and their train, enlarger of humility, discernment and dispassion; crown among kings and ornament of earth, give us devotion, the boat across the river of transmigration. You are the eternal swan on sages' mind-lakes, whose lotus feet Brahma and Shiva revere; banner of Raghu's line and bridge guarding revelation, devourer of time, karma, nature and qualities; vessel that bears us across, remover of every fault, ornament of the three worlds—Lord of Tulsidas.’

words.grammar: noun in the phrase ‘crown-jewel of kings’
words.sourceRef: Pinned numbered source, Uttara-kanda 35; common editions read मनि.

entries.meaning: Sanaka and the others departed for Brahma's realm, while the brothers bowed their heads at Rama's feet. They were all hesitant to ask the Lord and kept looking toward Hanuman, wishing to hear from the Lord's own mouth the words that dispel every delusion. Knowing their hearts, he said, ‘Hanuman, tell me what the question is.’ Joining his palms Hanuman replied, ‘Listen, compassionate Lord: Bharata wishes to ask something, but his mind hesitates to put the question.’ ‘You know my nature, Hanuman; is there any difference between Bharata and me?’ Hearing this, Bharata clasped the Lord's feet: ‘Listen, Master, remover of your suppliants' pain.’

‘Treasure of mercy, I shall take one liberty. I am your servant and you bring your people joy. Veda and Purana praise the greatness of saints in many ways, and you too have extolled them with your own holy mouth, for the Lord's love for them is surpassing. Ocean of grace, expert in virtue and wisdom, I wish to hear their characteristics. Protector of those who bow, explain clearly the distinction between saint and non-saint.’ Rama answered, ‘Brother, hear the qualities of saints, celebrated in countless scriptures and Puranas. The conduct of saints and the wicked resembles that of sandalwood and an axe: the axe cuts sandalwood, but sandalwood gives it its own virtue and perfumes it.’

‘Untouched by sense-objects, good in conduct and mines of virtue, saints grieve at another's grief and rejoice at another's joy. Even-minded and without enemies, free from pride and dispassionate, they abandon greed, anger, elation and fear. Tender-hearted and compassionate to the lowly, they cherish guileless devotion to me in thought, speech and deed. They honour everyone but claim no honour; such beings, Bharata, are as dear to me as life. Free from desire and devoted to my name, they are abodes of peace, dispassion, humility and joy; coolness, simplicity, friendship, love for Brahmins' feet and the power to engender dharma dwell in them. Know for certain, dear one, that whoever carries all these marks in the heart is always a saint. They do not waver from self-restraint, control, observance or right conduct, and never utter harsh words.’

words.grammar: compressed compound used predicatively of saints
alternatives: regarding no one as an enemy

entries.meaning: ‘Now hear the nature of the wicked; one should not associate with them even by mistake. Their company always causes pain, just as a bad cow ruins even a fine Kapila cow. The wicked burn with a special fever in their hearts, forever consumed at the sight of another's prosperity. Wherever they hear someone maligned, they rejoice as though they had found buried treasure. Devoted to lust, anger, pride and greed, they are merciless, deceitful, crooked and dwellings of impurity. They bear causeless hostility to everyone—toward benefactors no less than others. Falsehood governs their taking, giving, eating and every morsel. They speak sweetly like a peacock, but have a heart so hard that it would devour a great serpent.’

words.grammar: object of ‘devours’ in the peacock comparison
alternatives: very; exceedingly (literal sense of supplied अति)
words.sourceRef: Pinned numbered source reads अति; common editions read अहि.

entries.meaning: ‘Greed alone clothes them and spreads their bedding; they live only for sex and the belly and feel no fear of Yama's city. If they hear anyone praised, they sigh as though seized by fever. When they see another in distress, they become as happy as if they ruled the world. Absorbed in self-interest, hostile even to family, lustful, greedy and violently angry, they honour neither mother, father, teacher nor Brahmin. Ruined themselves, they bring others to ruin; delusion drives them to betray others, and they have no taste for saints' company or Hari's story. Oceans of faults, dull-minded and lustful, they mock the Vedas and seize others' wealth. They especially hate Brahmins and everyone else; inwardly full of vanity and deceit, they wear a fair outward guise.’

words.meaning: sex and the belly [source form सिस्त्रोदर]
words.grammar: compound naming sexual appetite and appetite for food
